## Pull request overview > [!NOTE] > Copilot was unable to run its full agentic suite in this review. This PR adds a new CUDA fast-path for `moe_align_block_size` targeting decode-like shapes with small batches and many experts, plus accompanying tests and benchmarks to validate and measure the new path. **Changes:** - Added `moe_align_small_batch_many_expert_kernel` and dispatch logic for `numel <= 1024` and `num_experts > 64`. - Added pytest coverage for small-batch/many-expert and boundary (fallback) cases. - Added a dedicated benchmark mode (`--small-batch-many-expert`) for decode-like many-expert configurations. ### Reviewed changes Copilot reviewed 3 out of 3 changed files in this pull request and generated 5 comments. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | tests/kernels/moe/test_moe_align_block_size.py | Adds parametrized tests covering the new fast-path and fallback boundary. | | csrc/moe/moe_align_sum_kernels.cu | Introduces a new CUDA kernel and dispatch condition for small-batch many-expert shapes. | | benchmarks/kernels/benchmark_moe_align_block_size.py | Adds benchmark configs + CLI flag to measure the new decode-like shapes. | --- 💡 Add Copilot custom instructions for smarter, more guided reviews. Learn how to get started.

The kernel’s prefix-sum/termination logic implicitly assumes `num_experts < 1024` and also requires the existence of a thread with `threadIdx.x == num_experts` to write `cumsum[num_experts]` and `total_tokens_post_pad[0]`. This breaks for `num_experts == 1024` (no thread 1024 exists) and for any `num_experts > 1024` (only the first 1024 experts participate in the scan). A concrete fix is to either (a) tighten the fast-path guard to `num_experts <= 1023` and fall back otherwise, or (b) rewrite the kernel to compute `cumsum[num_experts]`/`total_tokens_post_pad` without relying on a sentinel thread (e.g., use an inclusive scan and have the last participating thread store the total), and handle `num_experts > blockDim.x` via tiled scans or a different scan strategy.

The new mode allocates dynamic shared memory proportional to `num_experts` (`(3*num_experts+1)*4` bytes) *plus* CUB BlockScan temp storage. For large `num_experts`, this can exceed per-block shared-memory limits and cause kernel launch failures. Consider adding an explicit upper bound in the mode guard based on (1) supported `num_experts` for the algorithm (see scan assumptions) and (2) the device shared-memory limit (or at least a conservative cap like `num_experts <= 512/768/1023` depending on expected GPUs), with a safe fallback to the existing kernel when exceeded.

Test name reads as singular ('many_expert') but the test targets many-expert configurations; consider renaming to `test_moe_align_block_size_small_batch_many_experts` for clarity and consistency.

`torch.randperm` defaults to `int64`, so assigning into an `int32` tensor likely incurs an implicit cast on each iteration. To avoid repeated conversions, construct the permutation with `dtype=torch.int32` (and optionally use a vectorized construction similar to `get_topk_ids`) so the test spends less time on dtype/loop overhead and more on validating the kernel behavior.
